h1: The 7 Best Steam Mops with Scrubbers for Stuck-On Messes in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Steam Mops with Scrubbers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 steam mops with powered or built-in scrubbers from Shark, BISSELL, PUREBEAR and more, compared on pads, steam and price.
summary: The Shark Steam & Scrub S8001 is the steam mop to buy if you want scrubbing power, with an all-in-one hard floor design that spins the pads while it steams. The S8002BRN is the same idea at a lower price, the BISSELL Spinwave SmartSteam adds swivel steering, and the PUREBEAR gives you a 13-piece kit with scrubbing.
intro: A steam mop softens dirt, but softened dirt still has to be moved, and a flat pad dragged across the floor does that poorly on baked-on spills. A scrubbing mechanism closes that gap. Powered scrubbers spin or oscillate the pads, which mimics a scrub brush. A built-in brush works only when you rock the mop. The difference is the reason to choose one type over the other.

So this ranking sorts seven steam mops by how they scrub: powered rotation, rotating pads, or a stationary brush. We then looked at steam control, pad design, weight and price. We reviewed listings and specification sheets, and we note where steam is risky on hardwood or laminate, because scrubbing and heat together are harder on finishes.

products.name: Shark Steam & Scrub Steam Mop, All-in-One Hard Floor Cleaner, Grey, S8001
products.verdict: Shark's most capable powered scrubbing design, with steam and pads working together.
products.description:
The S8001 is Shark's all-in-one steam and scrub hard floor cleaner, and the listing singles it out as the brand's most capable powered scrubbing design. It costs $100 to $200.

Powered scrubbing means the pads move for you, so you do not have to lean on the handle to shift dried-on spills. That is a real difference on kitchen floors, where sauce and juice bake in. It leads because it does the most work, though motors and moving parts add weight and cost.

Buy it if your floors collect sticky residue. Skip it if you want the lightest, simplest mop.
pros: Steam and scrub in one pass

products.name: Shark Steam & Scrub Hard Floor Steam Mop, Teal, S8002BRN
products.verdict: The earlier Shark Steam & Scrub, with powered scrubbing at a lower price.
products.description:
The S8002BRN is the earlier Shark Steam & Scrub hard floor mop, aimed at buyers who want powered scrubbing at a lower price. It costs $100 to $200.

It gives you the same core idea as the S8001, with powered pads and steam, but the listing offers fewer details on upgrades. It ranks second because it is the more affordable route into powered scrubbing and shares the brand's pad system. The caveat is that it may be an older design.

Buy it if you want powered scrubbing without paying for the newest model. Skip it if you want the latest design.

products.name: BISSELL Spinwave SmartSteam Steam Cleaner Mop, Swivel Steering, 3897A
products.verdict: Spinning pads with swivel steering that eases navigation around furniture.
products.description:
The SmartSteam 3897A is a Spinwave mop with swivel steering and powered scrubbing, at $100 to $200.

Spinning pads scrub as they travel, and swivel steering makes the head follow your hand around chair legs and corners. That combination suits furnished rooms where a stiff mop fights you. It ranks third because the listing gives few details about steam levels or pad types.

Buy it if you have furniture to steer around and want powered scrubbing. Skip it if you want documented steam control.
pros: Spinning pads scrub as you go

products.name: PUREBEAR 300F Scrub & Steam Mop, Steam Cleaner With 13 Accessories
products.verdict: A corded scrub and steam mop with a 13-piece accessory kit, at $50 to $100.
products.description:
The PUREBEAR combines scrubbing and steam in a corded design with 13 accessories, and steam at 300 degrees Fahrenheit. It costs $50 to $100.

It is the kit for someone who wants scrubbing and the ability to attack grout and surfaces beyond the floor. High temperature steam helps with greasy buildup. It ranks fourth because the brand is newer and the listing details are limited.

Buy it if you want scrubbing and a kit for under $100. Skip it if you want an established brand.
products.idealFor: Scrubbing and detail work on a budget.

products.name: Scrubbing Steam Mop with Rotating Pads for Floor Cleaning, Steam Cleaner F6
products.verdict: A budget steam mop with rotating pads for scrubbing action.
products.description:
The F6 steam cleaner uses rotating pads to scrub as it steams, and costs $50 to $100.

Rotating pads give a scrubbing effect without a heavy motor system, which keeps the price down. It ranks fifth because the listing is light on specifications and the brand has little track record, so check warranty terms.

Buy it if you want rotating pad action cheaply. Skip it if you want proven reliability.

products.name: Bissell PowerFresh Deluxe 1806 Steam Mop for Tile, Hardwood & Sealed Floors
products.verdict: A stationary scrub brush design with variable steam and a 30 second warm-up.
products.description:
The Deluxe 1806 offers variable steam levels, a fast warm-up of about 30 seconds and a stationary scrub brush for stuck-on spots. It costs $100 to $200.

The brush works when you rock the mop over a spot, which is simpler and lighter than a powered system. Variable steam is the real strength, since it lets you reduce moisture on wood. It ranks sixth because you do the scrubbing yourself.

Buy it if you want control and a light mop with a brush. Skip it if you want powered scrubbing.
products.idealFor: Careful cleaning of mixed hard floors.

products.name: Shark SteamSpot Steam Mop with Steam Blaster Technology, White, S2001
products.verdict: Steam Blaster Technology and a simple built-in brush instead of powered rotation.
products.description:
The SteamSpot S2001 uses Steam Blaster Technology and a simpler built-in brush rather than powered rotation. It costs $100 to $200.

The Steam Blaster delivers a burst of steam for stuck-on spots, and the brush does the scrubbing. It ranks last because powered or rotating designs scrub more with less effort.

Buy it if you want a burst of steam and a plain brush. Skip it if you want powered scrubbing.
products.idealFor: Spot attacks with steam and a brush.

whatMatters.detail: Powered pads move on their own and save effort, rotating pads spin as you push, and stationary brushes need you to rock the mop. Choose by how stuck-on your messes are. Heavier messes justify motors.
Scrubbing and steam together can wear down thin or damaged finishes. Check that your floor is sealed and steam-approved, and test a hidden area. Never scrub unsealed wood.
Scrubbing pads wear faster than flat pads and you may buy replacements. Check pad availability and price. Washable microfibre pads last longer.
Motors and tanks add weight, which you push or carry. A heavier mop with powered scrubbing can feel better on a floor, but worse on stairs. Check the stated weight.
Variable or multi-level steam lets you reduce moisture on wood. Fixed steam suits tile. Check the listing for adjustable levels.

faq.q: Do steam mops with scrubbers clean better?
faq.a: On baked-on spills, yes, because the scrubbing action moves loosened dirt. On light dust they are no better than a plain steam mop.
Scrubbing a delicate finish. Check that your floor is sealed and approved for steam, and keep the mop moving.

faq.q: Is the Shark S8001 worth it over the Deluxe 1806?
faq.a: If you want powered scrubbing, yes. If you value steam control and a light mop, the Deluxe is better.
Fill the tank, snap on the pads, plug in and wait for steam. Powered models may need pad alignment.

faq.q: How do I care for the pads?
faq.a: Machine wash them without fabric softener and air dry. Replace worn pads.

faq.q: Can I use it on hardwood?
faq.a: Only if sealed and approved. Prefer variable steam and avoid scrubbing worn finishes.

finalTake: For stuck-on messes, the Shark Steam & Scrub S8001 is the best steam mop with a scrubber here because the pads do the scrubbing for you. The S8002BRN is the cheaper powered alternative, the BISSELL Spinwave is the best around furniture, and the PUREBEAR adds a big kit. Keep a lighter option for wood.
